below describe. The vector is real and printing it is what the command is
for -- what was missing was anything to stop a reader taking `offset=0`
for a position.

The test holds both directions, which is what a conditional note needs: it
fails when the note is absent for a parameter, and fails again when the
note is printed for an ordinary member. Sabotaged both ways and watched to
go red on a different assertion each time.

### 26.400 A refusal test whose population went empty, and its two detectors

**The test that held the refusal was named for the cells it listed**, and
when the last of them learned to pass an argument, all three parameters
went red for the same reason: there was nothing left to refuse. A test over
an empty set reports success exactly as loudly as a real one, so deleting
it and shrinking it were both wrong.

**What replaced it asserts the partition.** Which generators refuse is read
out of `situc/codegen` rather than carried in the test, so a generator
added without either passing an argument or declining to is a failure
addressed to whoever added it. Beside it, a control that the five which
used to refuse now GENERATE -- which is what says a refusal was removed
rather than a test deleted.

**Both halves of the first draft were wrong, and the sabotage is what said
so.** Commenting out `refuse_parameters(schema)` in the differ left the
partition test GREEN: the detector read the file as text, and
`# refuse_parameters(schema)` matched the pattern it was looking for. **A
detector that cannot tell live code from a comment reports the very thing
it exists to notice the absence of.** It walks the AST for a `Call` now.

And the refusal-message test passed `"unit"` to `differ.generate`, whose
third argument is a TARGET. Under the sabotage it failed with a `KeyError`
rather than *did not raise* -- so it had never exercised anything past the
refusal, and would have gone on passing with the refusal moved anywhere
earlier in the function. **A test that fails for the wrong reason under
sabotage has not been shown to work**, which is why reading WHICH failure
came out matters as much as that one did.

### 26.401 A refusal message that outlived what it refused

`refuse_parameters` still told the user "no view carries one yet", and sent
them to "the view constructor, the walker's `acquire` and the dissector's
preference" as the missing work. By then all four view constructors and the
dissector's preference were built. **A live, user-facing diagnostic naming
finished work as the reason for a refusal** -- and the docstring above it
said the function served "all four backends and the packer", none of which
still call it.

The seven callers left are the generators that emit a SECOND artifact over
a schema: the differ, the C checks, fuzz and tamper harnesses, and the
three `derived` emitters. Each builds calls of its own that would have to
thread an argument through, and none is on a `situc build` path -- so what
a parameter costs there is `situc gen-checks` and its siblings declining,
which the message now says.

It is the same shape as the stale comment in Rust's `generate()` (26.398),
found the same afternoon, and the reason to write both down is that
neither was found by a gate. **A comment and a diagnostic are the two
places a claim can rot with nothing downstream to trip over**: no test
asserts what a refusal's prose says is missing, and the reader it misleads
is the one who has just been stopped and is looking for what to do next.

### 26.403 Both walkers take the argument, and where each one puts it

**The image carries it as `image_placement.text_flags` bit 6.** `flags` is
full -- all eight bits spoken for -- and `text_flags` had 6 and 7 free,
with `peek` already at bit 5 for exactly this reason: it is the
placement's SECOND flag byte rather than a text number's alone, and `peek`
is `parameter`'s nearest cousin, the other member that occupies nothing.
So the record did not grow, the stride did not move, and `situc map
--check` and `situc wire --check` both report `std/image.situ.map` and
`.wire` current -- verified here rather than taken from the report, and
neither committed file is touched. Which also means the `[stream]`
wire-compatibility question 26.391 leaves open does not arrive through the
image.

**The row still says `offset_bits` and `size_bits`, and that is why the
flag cannot be inferred.** Layout answers `offset = 0` -- where `body`
begins -- and `size = 8`, how wide the argument is. A walker without the
flag spends that byte and reads the next member's first byte as the
argument: the same fault as the accessors, arriving at the walker by the
same route.

**Python keys arguments by placement index; C keys them by ordinal, and
that difference is a hole in one of them.** `acquire(image, buffer,
struct, args=())` stores `{placement index: value}`, so another struct's
parameter is simply not in the map. The C walker has no view -- every
entry point takes `(image, message, len, shape)` -- so the arguments go on
the `situ_walk_image` binding, keyed by ordinal, and in a schema with two
parameterised top-level structs, acquiring for `one` and then reading
`two` returned ONE's argument. A number, not an error.
`situ_walk_image` records `arg_shape` beside the arguments now and
`argument_of` refuses a mismatch.

**Refused in four places and never defaulted**, including again at the
point of use -- so a `View` built by hand, which the sub-view paths and
the tests both do, cannot get a defaulted answer through the window
either. Python raises a new `walk.Unsupplied` rather than a `Refused`, and
C gets `SITU_WALK_ARGUMENT = 10`, because everything else in those modules
answers a question about BYTES and this is the caller's omission. That is
26.394's distinction: exit 2, not 1.

**Two sabotages first failed through the compiler rather than through the
check** -- `-Werror` on an unused static, then on a tautological compare
-- and were reworked until they failed through the check under test. That
is the rule about a control having to be REACHED, met twice in one file.

**And a `printf` trap cost two false readings.** `printf("%d %llu",
(int)situ_walk_read(..., &v), v)` reads `v` before the call that fills it
as readily as after, and both times it looked exactly like the walker
returning a wrong value. The committed driver sequences the read into its
own statement and says why.

**One deliberate non-change, recorded rather than taken:** `parameter` is
not in `pack.CONSTRUCTS` / `ENCODED`. That table lists side-table
FAMILIES, and `peek` and `scaled` are flags and are not in it either -- so
adding one flag and not the others would be the inconsistency rather than
the fix. Whether the coverage report should count flags is a question for
whoever owns that table.

### 26.402 The corpus struct costs more than 0050 says, and the tree has the precedent

**0050's remaining-work line says a corpus struct "lands with the
backends".** Measured, that is wrong: it lands with every generator that
SWEEPS the corpus, and four of the seven that still refuse a parameter do.

`test_generated_sources_follow_the_conventions.py` parametrizes over
`every_schema.SCHEMAS` -- which includes `test/schema/edges.situ` -- and
runs `c/checks.generate` and `c/fuzz.generate` on each. `fourway.py` runs
`differ.generate` over corpus schemas the same way. So a `parameter` added
to `edges.situ` today does not produce a gap in coverage; it produces a
`SituError` from a sweep that currently passes.

**Which is the whole argument for putting it there, arriving from the
other side.** A construct the corpus does not carry is one no gate can
fail on -- and the moment it carries one, four gates fail, which is those
gates working. What has to change first is not the corpus.

**The shape is already in the tree, in one of the four.** `c/fuzz.py`
filters the structs it cannot handle rather than refusing the schema:
byte-sized, non-register, non-zero-size. So the answer for a parameter is
the same -- skip the struct that takes one and say so, rather than decline
the file -- and it is a precedent to follow rather than a decision to
take.

**And that filter carries the warning to copy with it.** Its comment
records `example/protobuf` being filtered out entirely, leaving a harness
that compiled, ran under the smoke test, and exercised nothing: *16
million executions at coverage 1, which is what an empty
`LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` looks like from the outside.* A per-struct skip
that can empty the artifact has to fail rather than shrink.

Recorded rather than done: it is a behaviour change to five generators,
and entangling it with the view work would put two unrelated things under
one message. It is the next piece, and it is what 0050's corpus line
should say.

### 26.407 Skipping the struct rather than the schema, in checks and fuzz

**The corpus struct's first blocker, removed.** `c/checks` and `c/fuzz`
declined a whole schema carrying a `parameter`; they now skip the struct
that takes one and generate for the rest, following `c/fuzz.py`'s own
precedent -- the filter that already drops structs it cannot fuzz.

**The skip reaches FOUR families, not one, and that was measured rather
than assumed.** With the refusal bypassed, the emitted suite called
`situ_P_mode_get` -- which does not exist, a parameter getting no
accessor (26.398) -- and `situ_P_validate(view)` with the wrong arity,
and named the struct again from the relation, conversation and framing
families. So `checks` skips in `_struct_checks`, `_relation_checks`,
`_converse_checks` and `_frame_checks`, and `fuzz` skips in the struct
filter AND in `_relation_harnesses`, which calls the view directly and
never consults the struct list. **A skip written only where the first
symptom appeared would have left three families calling a function that
is not there.**

**The whole struct, not the members after the parameter.** The tail goes
on the accessors whose arithmetic reaches the argument and not the rest,
so a partial suite would be checking exactly the half whose signature
happens not to have moved -- a passing check over the wrong population.

**When the skip leaves nothing, the whole-schema refusal still fires**,
which is the `example/protobuf` lesson turned from a comment into a
guard: an empty `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` and a `test_nothing_to_check`
placeholder both compile, run, and report a pass over nothing. Keeping
`refuse_parameters` for that case also keeps one diagnostic rather than
two (26.401), and keeps both files inside the partition
`test_wellformed` asserts over -- so `REFUSING` did not have to change.

**The two sabotages worth keeping failed through the COMPILER with the
exact hazards claimed**: removing the skip gave *too few arguments to
function `situ_box_validate`* and *implicit declaration of function
`situ_box_n_get`*. Not an earlier step, and not a string assertion --
the two faults the skip exists to prevent, named by gcc.

**One honest imprecision, stated in the code:** `checks` cannot tell a
schema its skip emptied from one that had nothing checkable anyway.
Both refuse. Loud over precise; telling them apart would mean
generating twice.

**And one population assertion that is not yet a measurement.**
`test_every_fuzzable_struct_reaches_the_harness` now requires an argued
struct to carry a "No harness" note instead of a `fuzz_` entry -- but no
corpus schema declares a parameter, so that branch is unexercised by the
sweep. The real coverage is in the unit fixtures; the branch lights up
the day `edges.situ` gains the struct, which is the point of adding it.

### 26.408 A uniform tail is a rule with two halves, and only one was applied

**Three functions took an argument they had no business taking or no way
to name, and all three are the same half-applied rule.** 26.397 says the
C tail is uniform across `validate`, `check`, `required` and the offset
functions, so a caller has one shape to remember, and that a uniform tail
costs a `(void)arg_n;` wherever the body does not read it. The first half
was implemented in three places and the second in one.

- **`required` took no tail at all** in its fixed-size branch, so a
  meaning-only parameter left rung 4's reader passing an argument the
  header did not take.
- **The offset functions took the tail and never got the `(void)`**, so
  `situ_frame_tail_offset(view, arg_mode)` was an unused parameter.
- **The nested sub-view accessor took no tail** while embedding
  `situ_frame_hdr_offset(view, arg_n)`, so `arg_n` was undeclared.

**All three are invisible in the case the feature was built for.** A
`[stream]` parameter that sizes a member is read by the extent
arithmetic, by the offset terms, and by the base expression -- so the
conditional tail appears, the `(void)` is not needed, and everything
compiles. It is the MEANING-ONLY parameter, and the member placed AFTER
a sized one, that reach the other branch. The arc that built this
feature tested the construct it was built for.

**The nested one matters most, because an ordinary schema reaches it.**
`_argument_tail`'s docstring names two unplumbed shapes -- a run of
variable-sized structs, a delimited run's stride helpers -- and says no
schema in this tree has either, which was offered as reassurance. This
is a third, and `struct frame { parameter u8 n [stream]; u8 body[n];
head hdr; }` is a fixed header after a variable body: not exotic, just
absent from a corpus that carries no parameter at all.

**The definition and its caller now ask one question.** `_member_tail`
and `_member_args` both come from `_member_reads_arguments`, so the
signature and the call cannot disagree. Computing the tail from the
rendered offset separately in each place is precisely how two spellings
of one fact drift apart.

**A fourth shape was found, reproduced, and deliberately NOT fixed here
-- correctly, and for a better reason than the one given at the time.** A
variant ARM holding a nested struct is broken in more than one site, so
plumbing the sub-view alone turns *undeclared `arg_n`* into *too few
arguments* without making anything compile. A speculative edit to that
path was made and then reverted, on the grounds that **a change nobody
can prove is worse than an absence somebody has written down.**

**Closed by 26.430, as that entry says and as this one predicted.**
Re-measured 2026-09-25: a variant arm holding a struct that takes a
parameter is refused in C and C++ with *`held` takes an argument, so it
cannot be a member*, which is 0050's rule reaching an arm.

That reasoning held, and it was aimed at the wrong question. The shape
needed no plumbing at all: 0050 had already decided such a struct cannot
be nested, and the refusal simply was not reaching an arm. 26.430 closes
it as a refusal.

Found by the worker converting the per-layer generators, from minimal
reproductions, in a file that was not its own.

### 26.655 The cut, pass one: the tool, its proof, and the rate

26.608 measured the problem and left the pass authorised and undone. This
is the first one, and `tool/cut.py` is what performs it.

#### The measurement that shaped the method

716 entries, 43,002 lines, mean 60. **There is no small set of giants to
cut**: the largest 25 entries hold 10 per cent of section 26 and the
largest 200 hold 44, so the weight is spread and this is 716 entries of
reading, about 23 passes at pass one's size.

And the obvious mechanical key does not work. Keying on *"the paragraph
contains bold"* would drop 7,524 of 36,000 entry lines -- 21 per cent --
because almost every paragraph carries some emphasis. The rule is the
bold SENTENCE and the prose around it is the narration, which no regex
separates. So the cut is read rather than computed, and the tool's job
is the proof rather than the choosing.

#### Deletion only, which is what makes the proof mechanical

`CLAUDE.md` requires a mechanical change to state what must not change,
check it, and refuse to write when the check fails. So nothing is
rewritten and nothing is added, by whole paragraphs:

- **every heading survives, spelled identically and in order** -- an
  entry is cited by number from elsewhere, and a lost heading is a
  dangling reference somebody else holds;
- **every `N.NNN` reference that resolved still resolves**;
- **every retained line is a line of the original, in order**, proved as
  a subsequence rather than asserted.

A compressed paraphrase would read better and could not be checked. What
recovers a dropped paragraph is `git log -S` on its own words, which is
the property `evidence.md`'s cut relied on and the reason each pass is
one commit.

**All three were sabotaged and seen to fail**, which is the half a proof
needs most:

    heading removed    1 heading(s) changed or lost: #### The guard ...
    entry 26.35 gone   heading lost, and: 1 reference(s) now name no
                       heading: 26.35
    line rewritten     a retained line is not an original line, in order
    the pass applied   clean

#### Pass one: the fourteen phase entries, 388 lines to 223

26.0 through 26.13 are the implementation plan itself. For a COMPLETED
phase the deliverables list and the `**Acceptance:**` criteria are spent
plan -- neither a rule nor a number -- while the status, the caveats
carried forward and the rules are live. So 26.4 keeps its big-endian
compile-only caveat and 26.3 keeps *a predicate that quietly succeeds
because nothing implements it yet is worse than one that fails*, and the
"Implement X, Y, Z" and acceptance paragraphs went.

42 per cent off those entries, 849 headings intact, the docs gate green.

#### Two faults in the tool, one of which cost four lines

**The entry boundary was wrong.** A body ended at the next heading of
ANY level, so a `####` subheading terminated it: 26.654 listed four
paragraphs of nineteen lines, and the prose under its subheadings was
unaddressable -- which is where most of the narration in recent entries
sits. Bodies end at the next NUMBERED entry now. That also makes the
heading invariant reachable, where before no `--drop` could delete a
heading and the check could not be exercised through the tool at all.

**And I deleted four good lines testing the heading control**, by
passing `--drop 26.654:4` against a listing `head -6` had truncated, so
paragraph 4 was prose rather than the subheading I meant. Recovered by
reading `git diff --numstat` first -- 0 insertions, 170 deletions, all
mine, nothing rewritten and no other session's content in it -- then
restoring from HEAD and replaying the drop list, which is one command.

**That the pass is one reproducible command is why the mistake cost
nothing**, and it is the same argument as one-commit-per-pass arriving
from the other side: a cut that accumulates by attrition can be neither
replayed nor recovered.

#### The passes, one line each

Pass one's record was 130 lines about a 165-line cut, so the file GREW
by that commit. That is the weight 26.608 measured, reproduced in the
act of removing it. This entry is the method, written once; a pass is a
line.

	1  26.0-26.13   the phase entries     388 -> 223   -165
	2  26.628 .646 .636 .649  mine        533 -> 399   -134

#### And the structural move, which the holder chose instead

The projection below was put to the holder and the answer was to move
the cited entries to `doc/decision/`. The measurement that decides the
naming: section 26's entries are cited about 4,000 times, **2,652 of
them from source** -- `codegen/c/emit.py` alone cites 109 -- across 380
distinct entries, with 435 more cited from the document. So **a moved
record keeps its own number**, `26.NNN-slug.md`, rather than taking the
next in the `NNNN` sequence: renumbering would invalidate every one of
those sites, in code comments nobody would think to grep.

	move 1  the ten most-cited   48,865 -> 47,111   -1,754

`tool/split.py` carries the proof: every moved line lands in exactly one
record byte-identical, every heading stays in `project.md` over a
one-line pointer, and nothing else in the document changes.

**And the pointer check is the tool's, not the gate's.** `split.py` said
in its own docstring that the `docs` mode proves every pointer resolves,
which is false: `doc_paths` reads table rows only, deliberately, because
a path in prose is as often an example or a glob. The gate reported `4
path(s)` over a 47,000-line document and I read its "names no missing
file" as covering ten pointers it had never looked at. `--check` is the
check that sentence described, and it was seen to fail on a renamed
file.

**Two conflicts with that directory's convention, named rather than
resolved.** `harmonization.md`'s settled inventory spells a record
`NNNN-slug.md`, which `26.NNN-slug.md` deviates from -- forced by the
citations, and the inventory is the holder's to move. And the directory's
rule is that a record is *not edited once accepted*, where section 26's
entries are a living log: 26.648 was struck through and this entry
amended twice on the day they moved. Whether findings in that directory
are exempt from that rule, or the rule now bends, is the holder's.

#### What the cut will and will not reach, measured at pass two

**The yield is a property of the entry KIND, not of the reading.** A
completed phase's deliverables and `**Acceptance:**` criteria are spent
plan with a mechanical signature, and gave 42 per cent. Session-log
entries gave 15 to 20, because they were written as rules. The
signature is now exhausted: one `**Acceptance:**` paragraph, two lines,
remains in the document.

So the projection, which the holder should have before the other 21
passes are spent: the document is 80 to 85 per cent rule by its own
measure, the cut takes 7,000 to 9,000 lines over about 700 entries of
reading, and 49,000 lines becomes roughly 41,000 -- **still three
context windows.** The cut is worth doing and does not make this file
readable in one session.

What would is structural, and is not a cutting pass: splitting section
26, or moving the entries cited by number into `doc/decision/`, which
`harmonization.md` names as exactly the case a second document earns --
303 citations by number across two trees were what justified that
directory. **Whose decision that is, is the holder's**, and naming the
option with its cost is the whole of what this entry does with it.

### 26.654 A located accessor refuses an offset field the frame cannot reach

Set by the copyright holder, answering 26.653's open question: **the
located accessor refuses.** The walker was right and the four backends
were wrong.

What they did: `located_tail.spot` sits after a variable-length member,
so its offset saturates at the frame limit (`situ_advance_u32`), and its
getter is guarded -- `situ_in_bounds(view, offset, 1) ? load : 0`. Over
a 22-byte buffer the guard failed, the getter answered **0**, and
`payload at spot` served two bytes from offset 0:

    payload ok=1 len=2 first=234

234 is the buffer's first byte. So the accessor handed back real bytes
of the message under a name whose offset nobody wrote -- the plausible
number this repository rates worst, produced by a bounds check that
worked and a zero that lied.

#### The guard has to be on the READ

A zero that came from an unreadable field is indistinguishable from a
field that says zero, so nothing downstream can recover the difference.
C was already computing exactly the test needed, inside the getter, and
discarding its answer.

So each backend now refuses before using the offset, and three pieces
already existed:

- **`traverse.fields_named(struct, source)`**, new, returns the
  placements an expression reads -- the same question `_over_fields`
  answers when it substitutes a field, answered once because four
  backends needed the LIST rather than the rendering.
- **`_fits`**, in all four already, renders the bounds test and answers
  None for a field at a CONSTANT offset, which the check that acquired
  the view covers (20.2).
- **`readable_names` and `_names_a_field`**, which `fields_named` is
  built from.

**So the corpus split fell out rather than being arranged.** bmp's
`file.pixel_offset` is at offset 10 and gets no guard; edges' `spot` is
dynamically placed and gets one. The two located members in the tree
are exactly one of each case, which is luck worth naming: a corpus with
only bmp in it would have let this ship, since the guard that matters
is emitted for the shape bmp does not have.

    c       if (!(situ_in_bounds(view, situ_located_tail_spot_offset(view), 1u)))
    cpp     if (!(situ_in_bounds(raw(), situ_advance_u32(1, ...)))
    python  if not (self._len - (advance(1, ...)) >= 1):
    rust    if !(self.bytes.len().saturating_sub(situ_rt::advance(1, ...)) >= 1)

136 passed over the walker suite, the crafted-offset control and the
whole corpus differential, and mypy clean over 247 files.

#### The chain this closes

A probe held back for four interfaces (26.643) was built (26.652), found
the walker clamping where four refuse (26.653), and the holder's answer
then turned that into a fault in the four rather than in the walk. **The
probe's value was recorded in advance as "regression protection for code
that agrees" -- and the code did not agree.** That estimate was made by
reading all four located accessors and finding their bounds checks
spelled the same non-wrapping way, which was true and was about the
wrong line: the clamps agreed, and what the offset field answered when
it could not be read did not.

So a review that reads the four implementations of a check can still
miss the question, and the differential is what asks it. That is the
argument for the probe stated better than before it ran.

### 26.653 What the LOCATED probe found: the walker clamped where four refuse

`Probe.LOCATED` (26.652) went red on its first full gate, and not for
the reason I reported before measuring. Four failures, one cause each
time narrower than the last.

#### First: the walker's line had no `ok=`

    walker: 'pixels len=0 first=-1'
    C:      'pixels ok=0 len=0 first=-1'

The walker renders a located byte run through its generic byte-run path.
`report.py` gives it its own shape now, printing `ok=1` and `ok=0` on
refusal.

**Keeping `ok=` rather than dropping it from the probe was the decision
there**, and dropping it was the tempting fix: all five would have
agreed at once. They would have agreed by no longer asking. Without that
field a REFUSAL and an accepted EMPTY run print identically, and which
of the two a located clamp returns is the whole question.

#### Second: it clamped where all four refuse

    walker: 'pixels ok=1 len=0 first=-1'
    C:      'pixels ok=0 len=0 first=-1'

`report._run_bytes` ends in
`view.buffer[first:min(first + want, view.limit)]`, and its docstring
says why: a count the MESSAGE gives is an attacker's claim, so it is
clamped to what the frame holds -- 26.35's fix, after an accessor handed
a caller fifty-five bytes out of a five-byte frame.

**A located run is the other shape.** There the OFFSET is the
attacker's, and every backend refuses: `n > size || at > size - n` in C,
C++ and Rust, `at + n > len(buffer)` in Python. Measured on the failing
buffer -- `pixel_offset = 775173163`, `image_size = 1161049669`, over 62
bytes -- the walker's slice came out empty and it reported an accepted
empty run where four refused.

Two faults in that one line, and the second would have outlived the
first: it bounded by `view.limit`, this frame, where a located offset is
measured from the MESSAGE. A nested located member would have disagreed
even once the clamp was right. The located branch refuses and bounds by
`len(view.buffer)`.

**`walk.read_bytes` was already correct** and refuses this case -- I
checked it directly and it raised. The fifth column was getting its
answer from `report._run_bytes` instead. So the walker had two readers
for one question, one agreeing with the backends and one not, which is
`working-practice.md`'s *a value with two consumers where only some are
wired* in the reader rather than in the writer.

#### Third: I reported the cause before measuring it

The `ok=` fix was real and was not the fault. I said it was, in as many
words, and the next run corrected me -- then the run after that
corrected the correction, because the edges case was a third thing
again. Three failures, three different causes, and the first two
diagnoses were each confidently stated from a diff.

The habit that would have caught it is the one this session keeps
re-learning: the probe PRINTS the disagreement, and reading the printed
line costs one command. I reasoned about the emitter instead, twice.

#### And the precedent was in the entry I was closing

26.641 held the struct-run count probe back on exactly this -- turning a
probe on asks the WALKER something it does not answer -- and 26.642 is
the entry that closed it. I ran the differ suites, the partition test
and the random-bytes differential, and not `test_walker.py`, which is
where the fifth column lives. **The lesson was in the entry I was
working against**, which is a stronger failure than not knowing it: a
probe's two halves are the drivers and the walk, and that is now twice.

### 26.652 The LOCATED probe, and the control that refused to fire

The last of 26.641's list. `Probe.LOCATED` asks what four backends say
about a byte run placed at an offset the message chooses --
`name ok=<0|1> len=<n> first=<byte|-1>`, shaped like `ARM_BYTES`'
because the accessor is fallible in three of the four.

26.643 called this *a gap with a reason* and the reason was real: one
question, four interfaces.

    c       situ_<s>_<m>_view(&msg, view, &held)   fills a situ_view_t
    cpp     view.<m>(msg.raw(), held)              fills ::situ::rt::bytes
    rust    view.<m>(&raw)                         Result<&[u8]>
    python  view.<m>                               memoryview property, raises

C's branch is the only READ probe in that file needing `&msg` as well as
the view, which is the whole of what makes this member a different kind:
its bytes are at an offset in the message rather than in the frame.

The ask is narrowed to byte runs -- every located member the corpus has,
`bmp.bitmap_file.pixels` sized by a field and
`edges.located_tail.payload` a fixed `u8[2]`. A located scalar or struct
would want its own shape, and asking for one emits a driver that does
not compile, which is a schema nobody compares rather than a question
nobody asks.

`LOCATED` came out of the partition test's exemption table in the same
change, that table asserting in both directions.

#### The control refused to fire, which is the finding

Sabotaging C's clamp to the wrapping form `at + n > size` left the
random-bytes differential **green**. The sabotage was in the generated
code -- checked, not assumed -- so the probe ran and the four agreed
anyway.

The arithmetic says why. The wrapping form is wrong only when the sum
lands back inside the buffer: `at + n` in `[2^32, 2^32 + size]`, which
for a 60-byte buffer is **61 values out of 2^32**, about 1.4e-8 per
draw. Forty-eight random buffers per schema will never see it.

**So the probe guards agreement and cannot guard this answer.** A
differential over random bytes finds faults whose wrong inputs are
common; a clamp's wrapping window is the opposite shape -- astronomically
rare and perfectly reachable on purpose. The two need different
instruments, and the probe alone would have been recorded as protection
it does not provide.

#### What was added instead, and proved in both directions

`test/unit/test_a_located_offset_that_wraps_is_refused.py` crafts
`pixel_offset + image_size` to be exactly 2^32 over `bmp`, whose `u32`
offset field is the only one in the corpus wide enough to reach it --
`edges`' is driven by a `u8` and cannot.

    correct clamp    all four: pixels ok=0 len=0 first=-1
    wrapping clamp   c: BuildFailed -- the driver DIES

The wrapping form does not disagree, it crashes: C accepts the offset
and the probe reads at `base + 0x80000001`. `fourway.answers` counts a
driver that dies as part of its answer, which is why that is caught
rather than silent.

**The test pins the VALUE, not the agreement.** Four backends that all
adopted the wrapping form would agree with each other about a buffer
they should all refuse, so asserting agreement alone would pass. That is
`evidence.md`'s *break the symmetry, not a side of it*, and it is the
difference between this test and the probe beside it.

#### Why it was nearly recorded as working

The differential went green for `bmp` and `edges` the first time it ran,
and the probe lines were there in all four drivers. Both facts are true
and neither is the claim. **Stopping there would have published a probe
that cannot fail** -- the same vacuous pass as 26.645's sweep, in the
session that wrote the entry about it, and the second time the shape
has appeared in my own work rather than in the tree's.

69 passed over the differ, partition, random-bytes and this new suite,
and mypy clean over 247 files.

### 26.651 `required` saturates at the type's maximum, and the cast that would have lied

Set by the copyright holder, answering 26.649: **`required` saturates at
the type's maximum and keeps its old behaviour.** A `u32` length of
0xFFFFFFFF makes `need` 0xFFFFFFFF again, not the leaf-bounded
0x80000004.

The reason the holder's answer is the right one, stated so a later pass
does not re-derive it: 14.2b's leaf bound exists so that four backends
PLACE a member identically. `required` places nothing -- it reports a
byte count to a caller -- and for that the two bounds say different
things. 0x80000004 is two gigabytes, which a caller CAN satisfy, and
would then be handed a body truncated from the four the message
declared. 0xFFFFFFFF is a need nobody can meet, which is the honest
reading of a length nobody can meet.

#### How it is expressed: one flag, one caller

`leaf_bounded` threads through `_length_expression` ->
`_raw_length_expression` -> `_content_length_expression` ->
`_count_expression` -> `_count_read`, defaulting True, and `required`
is the only caller that passes False. It drops the BOUND and keeps the
CLAMP, which is the whole distinction: the result saturates at the
type's maximum instead of the leaf's.

    at = situ_need_u32(at, (uint32_t)situ_nonneg_u32(
            situ_saturate_i64(situ_get_be32(situ_base(view) + 1u))));

#### The cast that would have lied, and why a compiler could not say so

Dropping the bound broke five generated-code compiles at once:
`nonneg` takes `i64`, and the `as u64` and
`static_cast<std::uint32_t>` casts in the emitted text were there to
feed `leaf_u`'s parameter. **The obvious repair is wrong and nothing
would have reported it.** A plain cast to the signed type turns a
varint a lying message sets to 1.6e19 NEGATIVE, and the clamp after it
reads zero -- so `required` would answer "five bytes" for a message
claiming nine exabytes. That is 14.2b's own named failure, arriving by
the one path that deliberately declines 14.2b's bound.

So the two paths differ only in WHERE they saturate, and the unbounded
form is a sibling call rather than a cast: `situ_saturate_i64` in the C
runtime, `saturate_i64` in `situ::rt` and `situ_rt`, each widening a
`u64` to `i64` saturating at the signed maximum, with the caller's
`nonneg` carrying it to `UINT32_MAX`. Listed in `RUNTIME_SYMBOLS` as
part of the same change, that omission having cost a red 63-minute gate
earlier in this session.

**The transferable shape: a type error is a question, not just a
breakage.** Five compiles failed and the quick fix was one token. What
the failure was actually reporting is that the cast had been carrying
the bound's saturation all along, so removing the bound removed a
saturation nobody had named. A fix that satisfies the compiler would
have passed every test in this tree.

#### And Python stopped agreeing, by a route the bound had hidden

`required` accumulated with a plain `at += length` there, where C uses
`situ_need_u32` and Rust `saturating_add`. Python's integers do not
overflow, so its total simply grew past `u32`: `5 + 0xFFFFFFFF` is
0x100000004, a need the other three cannot express. It now emits
`at = min(at + length, 0xFFFFFFFF)`.

**That asymmetry predates all of this and was invisible while the bound
held.** Every length was capped at `LEAF_MAX`, and `5 + 0x7FFFFFFF`
fits in a `u32`, so the missing saturation never showed. Removing a
bound exposed a missing saturation, which is this session's other
findings run backwards -- bounds ADDED exposed missing clamps in
26.645, 26.646 and 26.650, and a bound REMOVED exposed this. Both
classes were hidden by the arithmetic staying inside its type for every
input anybody had tried, which is the property a differential over
hostile inputs is for.

1692 passed over the four codegen suites plus codecs and checks, with
no failures.

### 26.650 The last unclamped sum, and a reachability claim I got wrong twice

26.648 left `preserving` open as *"a sum in 32 bits, which is safe for
one clamped term and not for two"*, and 26.649 repeated it. **Both
statements were wrong, in opposite directions, and measuring took one
command.**

Across all 45 schemas in the tree, every `coded` and `sealed` region:

    kind=preserving  variable members=0   x4
    kind=preserving  variable members=1   x5
    kind=ratio       variable members=0   x1
    kind=ratio       variable members=1   x1

**No region anywhere has two variable members**, so the condition I
named cannot arise. And one variable member is not safe either, because
`inner` is `constant + (length)` and four of the five carry a nonzero
constant:

    keystore.situ  keystore            constant=32  plaintext, stride 1
    packet.situ    packet              constant=22  body,      stride 1
    edges.situ     sealed_run          constant= 2  vals,      stride 2
    edges.situ     sealed_self_sized   constant= 2  n, a varint's own bytes

A length that has saturated to `UINT32_MAX` makes `32 + length` wrap to
31 in `uint32_t`. So the danger is a nonzero constant and ONE term, not
two.

**Then the third measurement contradicted the second.** For a term to
reach `UINT32_MAX` it has to be a saturating product, and none of these
can be:

- a stride-1 run's length is the clamped count itself, at most
  `SITU_LEAF_MAX`, and `32 + 0x7FFFFFFF` fits;
- `sealed_run` is the only stride-2 case, where `count * 2` could reach
  `0xFFFFFFFE` and `2u +` that is exactly 2^32 -- **but its driver is
  `u8 n [max = 4]`**, so the term tops out at 510;
- `sealed_self_sized`'s variable member is a varint measured by its own
  bytes, at most 9.

So the sum is **structurally able to wrap and unreachable in this
corpus**, and it is one schema edit from being reachable: widen
`sealed_run`'s `n` to a `u16` and it is live.

#### The lesson is about the shape of the claim, not the arithmetic

Three successive statements -- safe with one term, unsafe with one term,
unreachable with one term -- and only the third was measured. The first
two were derived from reading the code, which is exactly what makes them
convincing: each followed correctly from the line in front of me, and
each was answering a question about the CORPUS that the line cannot
answer. `evidence.md`'s *a claim about another tree is a measurement you
did not take* is usually read as being about other repositories. The
same thing happens one function away.

What the measurement cost was one script over 45 files. What publishing
the unmeasured version cost was two entries and a paragraph to the
holder that had to be retracted.

#### Fixed anyway, and why that is not inconsistent

`preserving` now clamps where it has a variable term, in all four
backends, although nothing reaches it. Two reasons, and neither is
tidiness:

- It was the last arithmetic in `_region_length` outside the clamp.
  *An exception wider than its reason is how a rule stops being
  enforced* -- `code-style.md`'s sentence about an ASCII check, and the
  shape is the same here.
- The gap is a `u8` away. A finding whose reachability rests on one
  attribute of one test schema is not a property of the design.

**And the same pass found a real gap in the fix of 26.646.** C++ and
Rust built their wide form as `static_cast<std::int64_t>(inner)` and
`((inner) as i64)` -- a cast applied to the whole sum, which widens a
value the 32-bit addition has already wrapped. The `ratio` instance
that was measured had `constant = 0`, so it could not show this. Each
term is widened on its own now. That is the same rule failing one step
earlier than where it was fixed, which is the third time this session
that *a clamp bounds only the arithmetic it encloses* has located a
defect -- and the first time it did so in my own patch.

### 26.649 The walker reports the declared count, and 26.642's blocker was not real

Set by the copyright holder, answering 26.648: **the walker reports the
count the message declares.** `sized_run_count` returns the driving
expression's value, bounded `min(max(count, 0), 0xFFFFFFFF)` -- the same
two lines `size_bits` carries, and for the stated reason, that this
walker evaluates in Python and cannot overflow, so the bound is there to
agree with the three backends that can.

Nothing is left unbounded by it. Every element accessor checks its own
read, so a declared 32 over a buffer holding 2 yields two elements and
then refusals, which is what a reader needs to be told rather than a
count quietly trimmed to the truncation it found.

#### `nothing in the image says which` was true of the field and false of the program

26.642 could not take the declared count because `size_code` is a number
of ELEMENTS for a counted run and BYTES for a `[remaining]` one, and it
recorded that nothing distinguishes them. That held for the field's
value. It does not hold for the program the field points at:

| form | the program opens | reads as |
|---|---|---|
| `parts[remaining]` | `REMAINING, END` | bytes |
| `parts[n]` | `FIELD 4, END` | elements |
| `parts[n + 1]` | `FIELD 6, PUSH 1 ...` | elements |
| `parts[remaining / 2]` | `REMAINING, PUSH 2 ...` | **elements** |

Measured on four one-line schemas before anything was built on it.
`_sizes_in_bytes` asks whether the program **is** `REMAINING` -- two
bytes, opcode then END -- rather than whether it mentions it, and the
last row is why: a test that merely looked for the opcode would take
`remaining / 2` for a byte count and divide by the stride twice.

It also matches the compiler, which decides the same thing
syntactically: the parser makes a bare `remaining` into `sized_by` and
`remaining` inside arithmetic into a `size_expr`, and all four backends
branch on that. So the walker now draws the line where situc draws it,
rather than where the image's ambiguity forced it.

**The transferable part is the shape of the wrong claim.** 26.642 did not
guess; it measured, and its measurement was of the wrong artifact. An
ambiguity in a VALUE says nothing about the PROGRAM that produced it, and
the entry generalised from one to the other in a sentence -- *nothing in
the image says which* -- that reads as exhaustive and was about a single
field. A claim of the form "nothing here distinguishes X" is worth
re-reading for which "here" was searched.

#### Which uncovered a second defect, invisible by construction

`size_bits` multiplied `size_code` by the element width for a bare
`[remaining]` run -- where `size_code` is already bytes. The extent came
out inflated by exactly the stride, and `sized_run_count` then divided
by the stride and reported bytes as a count: 4 for a four-byte run of
two-byte records, where the backends divide and say 2.

**No test could have caught it.** Every bare `[remaining]` run in the
corpus is `u8`:

    u8 rest[remaining];        edges, x7
    u8 payload[remaining];     edges
    u8 content[remaining];     edges, x2

and at a stride of 1 the inflation factor is 1, so `count * 8` is the
right number of BITS by coincidence. A `u16` run or a run of records is
the shape that breaks and the corpus has neither -- confirmed by
searching for both. So the bug sat behind a factor that is only ever
one, in the one corpus that could have exercised it.

Fixed with the same discriminator, and the four forms now agree with
what the backends compute.

#### What it fixed, measured

`test/unit/test_walker.py`: **92 passed, 3 skipped**, where the gate at
`3fff69f` had it failing three ways. All three were the one cause:

- `test_the_walker_agrees_with_the_compiled_backends[ble/ble.situ]` and
  `[schema/edges.situ]`, the two disagreements 26.648 recorded;
- `test_the_writes_are_compared_at_all`, which had dropped to 29
  contributing schemas against a floor of 31. **The two that fell out
  came back with the declared count**, which is the answer to the
  question 26.648 left open about which they were -- they were not a
  separate regression at all. A count that stopped at the extent left
  the members past it unwritable, so the replay for those schemas
  declined and the coverage floor caught it. The floor existing is why
  that was a measurement rather than a guess.

One more thing the timings say, since two runs of this were abandoned
to a wall-clock bound before any of it was known: `test_walker.py` is
143 seconds and `test_walker_c.py` is the eighteen-minute half, because
it compiles a probe per schema. Bound them separately rather than as a
pair.

### 26.648 ~~The gate is red at the tip~~, and one of the twelve is a design question

**Closed.** `make check` at `571b522` is `MAKE_RC=0`: 8721 passed, 75
skipped, 49 minutes, and all three cross stages ran -- host, aarch64
little-endian under qemu, aarch64 big-endian compile-only. Pushed, so
`master` carries every commit below. The twelve failures recorded here
are all answered: the stale assertions re-quoted and the control
re-aimed in 26.649, the walker's count settled by the holder in the
same entry, the write comparison back to its floor by the same change,
and `required` settled in 26.651. The heading keeps its original words
struck through rather than rewritten, because the entries that cite it
cite that sentence.

`make check` on the pinned worktree at `3fff69f`: **`MAKE_RC=2`, 12
failed, 8709 passed, 75 skipped, 46m35s.** Only `a35e1a2` is pushed.
26.647's table lists four fixes as though all four had landed; they are
committed and the last three are not gated green. This entry supersedes
that reading.

The twelve fall into three classes and only the first is bookkeeping.

#### Stale expected text, eight of them

The count and region-length emission changed, so assertions quoting the
old spelling fail. `test_opaque_length_is_a_byte_count_not_an_element_
count` wants `return (uint32_t)(situ_get_be16(situ_base(view) + 0u));`
and now gets that wrapped in `situ_nonneg_u32(situ_leaf_u64(...))`; the
test's *intent* -- bytes rather than elements -- still holds. The
others are the same shape in `test_codegen_c.py`, `_cpp`, `_rust` and
`_python`, including `test_a_varint_may_size_an_array`, whose Rust
assertion quotes `self.n_value() as usize` verbatim.

These want re-quoting against the new emission, with the clamp named,
rather than relaxing to a substring that would stop testing the thing.

#### A sabotage control that can no longer fire

`test_a_run_length_that_stops_clamping_is_caught` corrupts an emitted
line to prove the check it guards would notice. Its target was

    return situ_min_u32((uint32_t)((uint8_t)(situ_base(view))[0u]),

and no such line is emitted any more, so the test failed on its own
`assert applied, "nothing to corrupt"` -- which is the guard the file
was built around, working. **A control whose corruption target moved is
a control that has silently stopped controlling**, and this one said so
out loud because somebody wrote that assertion. Re-aim it; do not
delete it.

`test_the_writes_are_compared_at_all` is the same kind from the
coverage side: *only 29 schemas contribute a write comparison, down
from 31*. Two schemas stopped contributing and the guard names the
reason it exists -- the total can be met by one schema writing more.
Unmeasured: which two, and whether the count ask is what dropped them.

#### The walker and the backends disagree about what a count IS

The real finding, and it is not the clamp.

    ble.situ   ('le_advertising_report', 'reports')
       walker: reports count=2        C: reports count=32
    edges.situ ('segments', 'parts')
       walker: parts count=0          C: parts count=234

With the ask on, a struct run's count is compared against the walker
for the first time. The walker answers **how many elements fit in the
extent**; C answers **what the driving field says**, clamped at the
leaf. Both are defensible and they are different questions.

**And the chain that produced it is the lesson.** 26.641 held the probe
back on two obstacles. The first was that the walker had no count for
five such runs, and 26.642 closed it by taking the count from the
extent -- a choice made with care and with its own measurement of what
`size_code` means. It could not be checked against the backends,
because the second obstacle was that the backends disagreed with *each
other*. So the first obstacle was closed by a decision the second
obstacle made untestable, and fixing the second is what finally asked
the question.

That is worth more than the defect: **two blockers on one probe were
not independent.** Clearing one of them under the other's shadow
produced an answer nobody could check, and it looked finished.

Which answer is right is a question for the holder, and 26.644's rule
says to look for it elsewhere in the project first: 0032's closing
invariant -- *no rung invents a fact the schema did not state* --
argues for the declared count, since "how many fit" is derived and the
element accessors bound each read anyway. That is an argument, not the
decision, and `sized_run_count` would be the thing to change.

#### What the next session does

1. Re-quote the eight stale assertions against the new emission.
2. Re-aim the sabotage control, and measure which two schemas left the
   write comparison.
3. Settle the count question, then gate `3fff69f` again and push.

Nothing is lost if that order slips: `a35e1a2` is pushed and green, and
every commit after it is local.

### 26.647 Fold: four clamp-once fixes, and the probe that found three

One session, one class of defect, found by turning on a probe that two
earlier entries had held back. The ladder, newest first:

| commit | what it fixed |
|---|---|
| `3fff69f` | a region's length arithmetic, wide and clamped once |
| `f7a090a` | the struct-run count ask turned on, flag renamed |
| `3d77ce5` | `_count_expression` split, one clamp at the exit |
| `a35e1a2` | the arithmetic count path's leaves bounded |

`tool/sweep.py --all --shard 0/120` went from `agreed 73, disagree 2`
to `agreed 75`, and a disjoint second shard (`1/120`, 75 more cells) is
also clean -- 150 of the 9000 with the probe on and nothing left to
answer for.

#### The one sentence worth carrying out of it

**A clamp bounds only the arithmetic it encloses.** Three of the four
faults were that sentence in a different place: a leaf unbounded before
a sum, a sum unbounded before a cast, and a clamped length multiplied
afterwards. 14.2b has said *bound every leaf, arithmetic signed in 64
bits, clamp once* since it was written, and every one of these was that
rule applied to the expression somebody was looking at rather than to
the expression that reached the caller.

#### What the instruments did, which is the other half

- **The probe could not be held back and trusted at the same time.**
  With the ask off, nothing reads a struct run's count, so a sweep of
  all eighteen cells with that shape reported `agreed 18` over a fault
  I had already read in the generated C and could not demonstrate.
- **My own write-up cited a vacuous pass as evidence** -- `sweep
  --only <cell>` reporting `agreed` while the probe was off -- in the
  entry recording a fix for exactly that. 26.645 carries the
  correction and the real control: probe on with the clamp in, agreed;
  probe on with C's clamp reverted, DISAGREE.
- **`--shard 1/120` without `--all` examined one cell** and printed
  `agreed 1, examined 1/1`. The number that would have caught it was
  on the line above.
- **C was the backend that looked right in every one of these.** A
  narrowing cast turns an implausible number into a plausible one, so
  the two honest backends read as the broken ones. Where four
  implementations disagree, prefer the absurd answer as the honest one.

#### How to stop this project's gate, measured here

The gate is `timeout 5400 make check` in a pinned worktree, run as a
background task. **Signalling the task's wrapper shell does not stop
it**: TERM on that bash left `timeout`, `make` and `pytest` alive and
reparented to init, which is `running-code.md`'s rule -- anything that
kills the supervisor rather than signalling the work leaves the work
running -- met from a third direction, after containers and
harness-kills.

What works is to find the `timeout 5400 make check` and signal that,
re-reading each `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` immediately before the kill
because a PID is a moment. Then check for orphans, `/tmp` (which is on
`/` on this machine, not a tmpfs), and deleted-but-open files. All
three were clear afterwards.

#### Open, with its measurement

- **A `preserving` region's length is still a sum in 32 bits.** It
  returns the inner terms unchanged, so one clamped term is safe and
  two could overflow between them. Unmeasured: whether a region with
  two variable members is reachable in the corpus. The other three
  kinds are fixed.
- The remaining items from 26.641 onwards stand: the `LOCATED` probe
  (four interfaces, no live defect), 0056's canonical decimal
  spelling, whether a literal-only struct gets a builder, 0043 versus
  the parser on `pad_to(n) [preserve]`, the three `_reserved_policy`
  copies in the non-C backends, and the `project.md` cut.

### 26.646 Two cells in seventy-five: the probe pays out twice more

26.645 said the probe could come on. Before turning it on I ran a real
shard of the composition space with it enabled -- `tool/sweep.py --all
--shard 0/120`, 75 of the 9000 cells -- and it disagreed on two.

Neither is the cell the probe was built for, and they are not the same
kind of finding, so both are recorded here and `HELD_BACK` stays
`False` until the first is fixed.

#### `--shard` without `--all` is one cell, not a slice

The first run I did was `--shard 1/120`, which reported `shard 1 of
120, 1 of 9000 cells` and examined one. The option strides `chosen`,
and `chosen` is a 40-cell random sample unless `--all` is given, so a
stride of 120 over 40 leaves one. The tool's own usage line says
`--all --shard 0/6` and I did not read it.

Worth the paragraph because of what the output looked like: `agreed 1`,
`examined 1/1`, exit 0. **A 1/120 shard that examines one cell reports
exactly like a 1/120 shard that passes**, and the figure that would
have caught it was printed on the line above. That is `evidence.md`'s
*a count inherits its detector* with the detector being my own
command line.

#### The bare-reference count path has the same hole, and the probe found it

`varint-count-rec-after-bytes-in-frame-constrained`, a struct run
counted by a bare `[n]` over a varint:

    c    : run count=1364443822
    python: run count=637019603630
    rust : run count=637019603630

The same two numbers as 26.644, one apart, and `1364443822` is again
`637019603630` modulo 2^32. 26.645 fixed the arithmetic branch of
`_count_expression` -- `sized_by is None and size_expr is not None` --
and that function has four other branches that return a count: the
`[stream]` argument, a varint driver, a scalar load, and digits through
`_text_count_expression`. None of them bounds anything. The varint one
is this cell:

So the fix is one clamp at the function's exit rather than four at its
branches, which is what 14.2b asks for in as many words -- *clamp
once*. `_count_expression` is now two functions in each backend:
`_count_read` answers the count and whether a message supplied it, and
`_count_expression` clamps when it did. The constant branches
(`array_count`, and the `[remaining]` division, which is derived from
the frame and already bounded by it) say so and are left alone.

Three things the restructure turned up that a per-branch patch would
have missed:

- **The `[stream]` argument is a leaf too.** It is caller-supplied
  rather than read (0050), so it is not a thing a message lies about
  -- but C's parameter is a `uint32_t` and Python's is an `int`, so a
  caller passing 2^40 makes the two disagree for the same reason a
  varint did. Bounded.
- **A signed scalar can drive a count**, and `leaf_u` over a negative
  one reads 1.8e19 and clamps to the top rather than to zero. Each
  backend now picks `leaf_i` or `leaf_u` by the driver's own
  signedness, which is what 14.2b means by *in the domain it was read
  in* and what a single helper per backend would have got wrong.
- **C++ ended every reading branch in
  `static_cast<std::uint32_t>`**, which is the same narrowing cast as
  C's and was the same non-bound. It read correctly in the one
  measurement that mattered in 26.644 only because that path was the
  arithmetic one.

Re-running the same shard with the probe on: `agreed 74, disagree 1`,
the one being the body fault below, which reproduces with the probe
off and against the pre-clamp emitters.

#### The other is older than the change and is not a count

`varint-arith-u8-after-delim-in-coded-constrained` disagrees with the
probe **off** as well, and disagrees identically against the pre-clamp
emitters at `95d8725`, so it is neither the probe's nor 26.645's:

**Measured, and it is 14.2b's own named failure, in the code, one
level out from the helper whose comment names it.** C emits

The `* 2u` is the `doubling` codec's expansion ratio, and it is applied
to the clamp's RESULT in `uint32_t`. Evaluating it over the sweep's own
buffer: the varint reads 637019603630, the leaf bound holds it to
`SITU_LEAF_MAX`, `+ 1` makes 2147483648, and `situ_nonneg_u32`
saturates at `UINT32_MAX` so that value passes through unchanged. Then
`2147483648 * 2` is exactly 2^32, which in `uint32_t` is **0** -- the
one product whose truncation is zero rather than merely wrong. So
`situ_min_u32(0, 45)` is 0, and the body is empty.

That is the arithmetic above, to the literal. The helper was fixed for
a multiplication INSIDE the clamped expression, and `_region_length`
then put one OUTSIDE it. **A clamp is only a bound for the arithmetic
it encloses**, which is the same sentence as the count path's *multiply
after clamping and the product leaves the domain again* -- written two
hours earlier in this session, about the path I was looking at, while
this one sat in the next function.

#### Where else the shape is

`_region_length` has four kinds and three of them do arithmetic on the
inner length: `ratio` (`* out / into`), `add` (`+ n`), and the group
form (`(inner + g-1) / g * g_out`). Only `preserving` hands the clamped
value through untouched. All three are in `uint32_t` in C and in
`std::uint32_t` in C++; Python's integers do not overflow, and Rust's
`usize` is 64-bit here -- which is why only C printed a wrong number in
a differential that compares all four.

C++ emits the same product (`(((0 + (::situ::rt::nonneg(...)) * 2) / 1)`)
at the decode call rather than in a length accessor, and Rust emits it
with an `as u32` on the end, which truncates the same way. Neither was
caught by this cell because the probe reads the span those backends
compute elsewhere, not the expression at the decode site. **Three sites
to fix, and only one of them is what the differential found** -- so the
other two are the ones that would have outlived it.

The fix is the shape 26.645 settled for counts: build the terms wide,
do the arithmetic in `int64_t`, clamp once at the end. Done, in all
four, and the cell agrees now -- every backend computes
`nonneg((wide * 2) / 1)` and answers 45.

**Python needed the change although Python could not get it wrong**,
and that is the part worth keeping. Its integers do not overflow, so
the product is exact there whatever the other three do. But all four
clamps saturate at `UINT32_MAX`, so once C, C++ and Rust clamp the
product they answer 4294967295 where an unclamped Python answers
4294967296. **The fix would have replaced a disagreement of four
billion with a disagreement of one** -- and a differential is at its
worst on those: a near-miss reads as a rounding question rather than as
the arithmetic failure it is, and the cell that found this one was
flagged by the size of the gap.

So the rule is not "clamp the backends that overflow". It is: a value
four programs have to agree about is clamped in all four or in none,
because **the clamp is part of the answer and not a safeguard around
it.**

#### The argument for the probe, restated with a number

26.641 held it back and 26.644 and 26.645 are what it produced. It has
now paid out three times: the arithmetic count path, the bare-reference
count path, and -- by making a shard worth running at all -- a
pre-existing C-only body fault that nothing else had reported. Two
disagreements in 75 cells is not a defect rate, since these 75 were
chosen by stride rather than for difficulty; what it is, is evidence
that the space has more of this in it than the one cell that started it.

### 26.645 The clamp on the count path, and the C cast that hid it

26.644 named the fix and said the walker needed none. Applied: the count
path in all four generated backends now bounds its leaves and clamps
once, which is what the length path beside it has always done.

What each emits for the cell `varint-arith-vrec-after-varint-in-frame-since`,
whose run is counted by `n + 1` over a varint:

    C       return (uint32_t)situ_nonneg_u32(situ_leaf_u64(situ_s_n_value(view)) + 1);
    C++     return ::situ::rt::nonneg(::situ::rt::leaf_u(n_value()) + 1);
    Python  return nonneg(leaf(self.n_value) + 1)
    Rust    situ_rt::nonneg(situ_rt::leaf_u(self.n_value() as u64) + 1)

#### What proved it, which is not the sweep

`tool/sweep.py --only varint-arith-vrec-after-varint-in-frame-since`
reports `agreed` both before and after the change, and that is not
evidence: with `HELD_BACK = False` nothing asks a struct run for its
count, so the sweep could not see this path at all. I wrote the sweep
line into this entry first and it would have read as a gate.

The control is the probe turned on, and it was run in both directions:

    probe on, clamp in all four         agreed
    probe on, C's clamp reverted        DISAGREE, count=1364443823
                                        against count=2147483648 x3

So the fix is proved by a check that fails when it is removed, which is
what `evidence.md` asks of a guard, and the sweep's verdict with the
probe off is a vacuous pass -- that file's first rule, met in my own
write-up of the fix for it.

It also corrects the numbers in 26.644. Those -- 637019603631 three
ways -- were measured with no backend clamping. With three clamped and
C not, the three answer 2147483648: the leaf saturated at
`SITU_LEAF_MAX` and then incremented. `situ_nonneg_u32` and its
siblings guard the low end; the leaf bound is what caps the high one,
and it is applied before the arithmetic rather than after.

**No `* element_bytes` on this path**, which is the one place it differs
from the length path it copies. A length is bytes and the clamp belongs
after the multiplication; this is a count of elements, and the clamp
belongs on the count -- multiply after clamping and the product leaves
the domain again.

#### The cast was the reason C looked right

Worth keeping because the appearance was the opposite of the fault. C
was the only backend whose number was inside `uint32_t`, so a reader
comparing the four would take C for the one obeying the rule and the
other two for the ones overflowing. It was the reverse: C's
`(uint32_t)` cast truncated 637019603631 to its low 32 bits and
produced a plausible count out of an implausible one. The two large
numbers were honest.

That is 14.2b's own text arriving a second time -- *"clamping the low
end alone left `(LEAF_MAX + 1) * 2` truncating to zero on the cast to
`uint32_t` -- the same failure one step along"* -- and the transferable
part is narrower than the rule: **a narrowing cast is not a bound, and
it is the one that makes a wrong number look like a right one.** An
unclamped count in C++, Python or Rust announces itself by being
absurd. In C it does not announce itself at all.

#### What it unblocks

26.641 held the struct-run count probe back on two obstacles: the C
macro for `edges.pieces.two[2]`, closed by narrowing the probe to runs
with no `array_count`, and this one. Both are closed, so `HELD_BACK` in
`situc/codegen/differ.py` can come on -- in its own change, gated
separately, because turning it on is what reproduces the red gate if
anything about either obstacle was wrong.

### 26.644 The count disagreement is not a decision: 14.2b already settled it

26.641 held the probe back partly on *"a decision about what a count
larger than the frame means"*. **There is no decision. The rule is
settled and no generated backend applies it on this path.**

14.2b, and the entry that states it here: *bound every leaf, in the
domain it was read in; do the arithmetic signed in 64 bits; clamp once,
saturating at both ends*, with `SITU_LEAF_MAX` at `INT32_MAX`. The
walker implements exactly that -- `min(max(count, 0), 0xFFFFFFFF)` --
and its comment says why in as many words: *"a lying varint has to
produce the same offset in all four, and a bound applied everywhere but
here is a disagreement waiting to happen."*

The count path in the three generated backends is that bound missing:

    C       return (uint32_t)(situ_s_n_value(view) + 1);
    Python  return self.n_value + 1
    Rust    (self.n_value() as usize) + 1

Over the cell `varint-arith-vrec-after-varint-in-frame-since` those
answer 1364443823, 637019603631 and 637019603631. **C's number is the
other two truncated**: 637019603631 mod 2^32 is 1364443823 exactly. So
C is not the one that applies the rule -- it is the one whose cast
hides the overflow, which is the failure 14.2b's own text names:
*"clamping the low end alone left `(LEAF_MAX + 1) * 2` truncating to
zero on the cast to `uint32_t` -- the same failure one step along."*

**All three are wrong, in three different ways, against a rule the
project wrote down and the walker obeys.** What makes it worth more
than a count is where that count goes: it places every member after the
run. A lying varint therefore puts them in three different places, and
the walker in a fourth.

#### Three times in one session

This is the third thing I recorded as the holder's decision that was
already settled somewhere else under another name -- after the readers'
count accessor (26.638, a bug with one answer) and `size_code`'s
meaning (26.643, answered by `size_bits`). `working-practice.md` names
the trap and the cost: *a wrongly-deferred question is caught by
nothing. It sits in the document looking exactly like diligence.*

What the three have in common is that **the deferral was written from
the diff rather than from the project.** Each time the evidence that
settled it was one grep away -- 14.2b for this, a `SIZE_FIXED` macro for
the accessor, `size_bits` for the field -- and each time I wrote the
entry while still inside the change that raised the question. The habit
that would have caught all three is the one `working-practice.md`
prescribes and I did not run: before deferring, search for the decision
under a different name.

#### What the fix is, and what it unblocks

Apply the leaf bound on the count path in all three backends, as the
length path already does: `situ_leaf_i64`/`leaf_u64` in C and the
matching helpers in C++, Python and Rust, arithmetic signed in 64 bits,
one clamp at both ends. The walker needs no change.

That closes 26.641's second obstacle, which means the struct-run count
probe can be turned on -- and the probe is what found this, which is
the argument for it rather than a cost of it.

### 26.643 The fifth count, and a field read three times before the right question

`walker/report.py` answers `count=` for a run the message sizes now --
`_sized_runs` as the complement of the four lists that existed, and
`walk.sized_run_count` beside the four counters. mqtt's two filter
lists, ble's reports, message's recs and edges' segments.parts are
counted, which closes the first of 26.641's two obstacles.

**The count comes from the EXTENT, and getting there took three
readings of one field.**

    first   `size_code` computes the member's byte extent        wrong
    second  it means elements here and bytes there, so the
            packer must record the unit                          too big
    third   the count follows from `size_bits`, which already
            resolves both forms                                  measured

The first was read off one call site and generalised. The second was
measured and true -- `size_code` evaluates to 12 for
`mqtt.subscribe_body.filters` over two six-byte subscriptions, where a
counted run's evaluates to a number of elements -- but it answered a
question nobody needed to ask. The third is that `size_bits` already
walks the elements for a variable run and multiplies for a fixed one, so
the extent is right for both forms and the count is the extent divided
by the element's size, or a walk inside it where the element has none.

**The lesson is not about `size_code`.** Each reading was a better
answer about the wrong field, and the right move was to ask what the
COUNT needs rather than what the field means. Two corrections published
in one session, both to my own entries, and the second one over-shot --
which is the direction a correction tends to go when it is written in
the same breath as the mistake it fixes.

A test asserts both sub-cases through `report._members` rather than
through the counter, for the reason the alignment test gives: a helper
that returns the right number and a renderer that never calls it are
indistinguishable from the lists.

**The probe stays off.** The walker gap is closed and the second
obstacle is not: the four backends still answer a count differently
where the message lies about it, C in `uint32_t` and the other two
wider, and which answer is right is a decision about what a count
larger than the frame means. `HELD_BACK` now carries one live reason
instead of two, with the closed half struck through where somebody
turning it on will read it.

### 26.642 What the walker needs for the fifth count, measured rather than guessed

26.641 held the struct-run count probe back partly because the walker
has no list for five such members. This is the diagnosis, so the next
session has an instruction rather than a question.

**The walker answers `count=` through four named selectors** in
`walker/report.py`: `_while_runs` for a `repeat_while` run,
`_record_runs` for a struct run ending at a terminator, `_tlv_runs` and
`_indexed_runs` for the two region kinds. A struct run the MESSAGE
sizes -- by a count field, by `remaining`, or by arithmetic -- matches
none of them, which is why the probe found nothing to compare against.

**The image already carries what a fifth selector needs.** Read from
the packed image for the three corpus cases:

    mqtt.subscribe_body.filters   size_code=set  element_bits=NONE
    message.message.recs          size_code=set  element_bits=64
    edges.segments.parts          size_code=set  element_bits=NONE

~~`size_code` is the code that computes the member's byte extent~~ --
**and that was wrong in the direction that ships a wrong number.**
Measured before the selector was written: for
`mqtt.subscribe_body.filters[remaining]` over a buffer holding two
six-byte subscriptions, `size_code` evaluates to **12**, which is the
remaining BYTES. For a counted run it is the ELEMENT count -- the extent
path proves it by walking `range(size_code)` elements. One field, two
units, told apart by the member's form and by nothing in the image.

**The extent path is insensitive to the difference and a count is
not.** For a `remaining` run it uses the byte number as an element
count and walks that many, stopping on `at >= view.limit` -- so the
extent comes out right by the loop's bound rather than by the number
meaning what the code assumed. A selector that returned `size_code` as
the count would have answered 12 filters where there are 2.

So the instruction is bigger than one selector in `report.py`. The unit
has to be knowable: either the packer records it beside the code, or the
walker inspects the code for `Op.REMAINING` (0x03) -- which is reading a
bytecode to decide semantics, and is the sort of thing to choose
deliberately rather than reach for. Where the unit IS elements the count
needs no walk at all, which is the one simplification this measurement
adds.

The selector itself is the complement of the other four:
`type_struct != NONE and size_code != NONE and repeat_code == NONE`,
excluding the delimited and region indices the three existing lists
already claim.

**Twice in one session a recorded conclusion needed correcting**, and
both times measurement caught it before code did: the readers' count
accessor called a decision when it was a bug (26.638), and this
entry's own claim about `size_code`. The common shape is a conclusion
drawn from reading one call site -- `walk.py` line 403 for the extent
-- and generalised to a field's meaning. **A field's meaning is not a
property of the first use you read**, which is the same error as the
branch-ordering family the writer increments kept finding, one layer
up.

#### The fourth instance of one pattern

Each of those four selectors carries the same sentence in its own
docstring -- *"the differ asks these `count=` and this walk answered
nothing"* for the record runs, *"the section existed and nothing loaded
it"* for `tlv`, *"written by the packer as `none` until 26.341 and
loaded by nobody"* for `indexed`. **Three selectors exist because the
same hole was found three times**, and this is the fourth, found the
same way: a probe asked and the walk was silent.

What makes it the fourth rather than the first is that nobody looked for
the complement. The four selectors are a list of shapes somebody met;
the question *which struct runs can the message size* has one answer and
it is in the layout, not in a list of cases. **A partition over that
question would have produced all five selectors at once** -- which is
26.640's argument about the probe list, arriving at the walker from the
other side, and is the shape worth taking to both.

### 26.641 The probe that found two things and is held back for both

26.639 added a `count=` probe for a run of structs, which nothing had
ever asked. The gate was red, and both reasons are findings.

**The walker has no list for five of them.**
`test_every_count_the_differ_asks_is_one_the_walk_answers` asserts that
every member the differ asks `count=` is one the walker's image can
answer, and it asserts it **over the schema rather than over a run** --
its own docstring says why, because `_by_member` compares only the keys
both listings have, so a line the walk never emits is skipped and the
differential passes. The five are `ble.le_advertising_report.reports`,
`message.message.recs`, mqtt's two filter lists and
`edges.segments.parts`. The probe was right to ask and the walker is
the fifth implementation that has to answer.

**And the four backends disagree about such a count when the message
lies about it.** From the composition space:

    varint-arith-vrec-after-varint-in-frame-since: disagree
      c     : run count=1364443823
      python: run count=637019603631
      rust  : run count=637019603631

A `vrec` run whose count is arithmetic over a varint the message chose.
637019603631 is past what 32 bits hold: C computes the count in
`uint32_t` and the other two in wider arithmetic, so a lying varint
produces three answers. **Which one is right is a decision about what a
count larger than the frame MEANS** -- the number the message states, or
what the bytes can hold -- and the differ's own comment names this class
in the sentence beside the probes: *the arithmetic is over ATTACKER
bytes*.

So `HELD_BACK = False` sits above `asks`, with both reasons written
there rather than in a commit message nobody will re-read. The
condition is unreachable and the code is not deleted, because what a
reader needs when they turn it on is exactly these two obstacles.

**That is the probe working, not failing.** It was added to close a
blind spot and it found, in one run, a fifth implementation that cannot
answer the question and a three-way split on an attacker-controlled
number. Both were invisible while nobody asked. The honest order is
walker first, decision second, probe third -- and none of them belongs
in the last hour of a weekly window.

#### What this cost and what it bought

One red gate, 65 minutes, after four suites passed locally. The suites
I ran covered the corpus and the differ's own tests; what caught the
divergence was the composition space inside `make check`, and what
caught the walker gap was a schema-level assertion nobody would think
to run by hand. **A local pass over the corpus is not a gate**, which is
the whole reason the gate exists -- and the reason to read a red one
rather than to narrow the thing that turned it red.

### 26.640 The probe list as a partition, and a detector that could not see the exempt case

26.639 ended by saying the differ's probe subset is worth auditing
against `traverse.classify` rather than grown by instalments. This is
that audit, as a test: every `Member` kind either reaches a probe or is
named with the reason it does not.

Measured over the corpus, 17 kinds occur and **15 are probed**:

    SCALAR 616 members   VARIABLE 81   ARRAY 55   DELIMITED 40
    NESTED 36   REGION 30   TAG 26   TEXT_NUMBER 16   REPEAT_WHILE 9
    VARINT 7   RECORD_RUN 4   CODED 4   MARKER 2   TLV 1   INDEXED 1

**Two are asked nothing, and they are not the same case.**

`RESERVED`, 58 members, is a real exemption: reserved bytes have no
accessor in any backend, their content being a policy rather than a
value, and the policy is what `validate` checks -- which every driver
already asks.

`LOCATED`, two members, is a gap with a reason. They are
`bmp.bitmap_file.pixels` and `edges.located_tail.payload`, both byte
runs whose POSITION comes from a field, which is where four independent
clamps are most likely to differ -- and BMP's are the pixel data every
reader of that format wants. What stops a one-line probe is that the
four expose such a run through four different interfaces: C emits
`situ_bitmap_file_pixels_view(msg, view, &out)`, taking the MESSAGE
because the offset is the message's rather than the struct's, while
Python gives a `memoryview` property. Comparing them needs a probe
shaped like `NESTED`'s, and that is the next piece here.

**And the gap is coverage rather than correctness, which was measured
before it was prioritised.** All four located accessors were read in
full, and all four spell the bounds check the same non-wrapping way:
`n > size || at > size - n` in C, C++ and Rust, and Python's
`at + n > len(buffer)` which cannot overflow because its integers do
not. The suspicion worth having -- that one of four independent clamps
over an attacker's offset had the wrapping form -- is false today. So a
`LOCATED` probe buys regression protection for code that agrees, not a
defect, and the next session can take it in that order rather than
re-deriving the four bodies.
